items.title: Windows Package Manager / Winget defaults to single-user installation
items.body:
I'm not sure if this behavior is deliberate or simply a consequence of the install wizard's default state being "For me (username)" rather than "For anyone who uses this computer (all users)"

Using the Windows Package Manager / 'winget' for scripted deployment, the installer is deployed in single-user mode.

Setting up an image for deployment to multiple systems, the installation is performed for the built-in administrator account and must be re-run once the end user has set up the device and created a user account.

If it aligns with the project's objectives, I propose having the .exe installer default to "all users" installation or, if possible, having the winget deployment include a variable to default to that method.

items.title: drop Python 3.8 and 3.9 support, require 3.10
items.body:
We will require Python 3.10 in general and Python 3.12 for Windows. This has a variety of benefits, including

- Drop support for EOL Python versions (3.8 and 3.9)
- Remove version conditions from requirements.txt
- Drop Python 3.9 in CI (or replace with newer version)
- Unix.py: Remove guard `hasattr(platform, 'freedesktop_os_release')`
- TestOptions.py: assertNoLogs
- windows/setup.py: remove exclusion for distutils
- Unlock Python 3.8 and 3.9 language features on all platforms
- Unlock Python 3.11 and 3.12 language features on Windows-specific code (e.g., is_junction)

[Recent comment](https://github.com/bleachbit/bleachbit/issues/1631#issuecomment-5553880220) about minimum Python version 

The implementation plan includes updating the version guard in `__init__.py` (3.10 always, 3.12 on Windows).

RHEL 9 / AlmaLinux 9, which use Python 3.9, have full vendor support through May 2027.  They can't simply use AppImage, though: it does not bundle Python interpreter. The AppImage could search for other Python versions installed, but they would need gi and other packages. High-effort options may not be feasible.

items.title: Failure to parse apt output if < 10000 bytes
items.body:
BleachBit's regex fails in the less common scenario of output smaller than 10,000 bytes. Example outputs from apt: `Del foo 1.0-1 [1234 B]` or `After this operation, 1234 B disk space will be freed.`

Notes

- This issue is a follow up to 0c9d1b7e41fb7fe2487700724bb46b589c18880d regarding parsing output of `apt`.
- apt's logic is in function `SizeToStr`in `strutl.cc`
- apt uses base 10 (not base 2)
- apt suffixes are 'k' (lowercase) and then 'M' through 'Y' (uppercase)
- We do not support Z or Y, which is not a real problem (especially in _this economy_ for storage hardware).
- We already set LC_ALL=C, so don't need to worry about localization for numbers.
- `apt` vs `apt-get` produce different strings
- Adding `-s` flag to `apt get autoremove` to simulate (dry run) skips the message, so it is not helpful.

## Normal usage (no bug)

Real-world procedure to reproduce output for autoremove with size >10000B (common):

```
sudo apt install -y mc
sudo apt remove -y mc
echo n | sudo apt autoremove # show without removing
sudo python3 bleachbit.py -c apt.autoremove
```

Example output from apt 3.2.0 on Ubuntu 26.04


Above outputs "After this operation, 9216 B disk space will be freed."

items.title: Replace Distro-Specific Installers For Linux With Universal Package Formats
items.body: Flatpaks, AppImages and Snaps are gaining a lot of popularity among most distros. Right now, BleachBit has way too many installers for Linux. It would be great if those could be replaced with one or more of the former package formats. It would make it much simpler for users to have one (or two) standardized way(s) of installing BleachBit on Linux and two of those three formats provide easy package management, which means users can have the latest version of BleachBit on their system. It would also reduce the burden on the development team while also making it available on most distros. Since Flatpak support is already on the way (#632), we are almost halfway there already.

items.title: BleachBit 6.0.3 — macOS Tahoe Apple Silicon Build & GTK Quartz Support + dmg installer
items.body: BleachBit 6.0.3 on macOS Tahoe Building a functional version for Apple Silicon (M4) Complete record of the successful procedure Python 3.8.18 · pyenv · GTK 3.24.52 · PyGObject 3.48.2 · GDK Quartz · Gettext · 61 languages · icon · ad-hoc signing PART 1 — Preparing the project The work was performed on the BleachBit source tree at ~/bleachbit. The version checked during the procedure was 6.0.3, on the master branch. cd ~/bleachbit git branch --show-current git log -1 --oneline python3 -c "import bleachbit; print(bleachbit.APP_VERSION) A dedicated Python 3.8.18 environment was created with pyenv: pyenv virtualenv 3.8.18 bleachbit-venv cd ~/bleachbit echo bleachbit-venv > .python-version pyenv version python3 --version which python3 The .python-version file makes pyenv automatically select the environment when entering the project directory. PART 2 — Installing Python and GTK dependencies The GUI requires PyGObject and GTK. GObject Introspection was verified through Homebrew and the required Python packages were installed in the virtual environment. pkg-config --modversion gobject-introspection-1.0 # 1.86.0 python3 -m pip install pygobject psutil requests Relevant final package versions: Successfully installed pycairo-1.26.1 pygobject-3.48.2 brew list --versions gtk+3 glib gobject-introspection # glib 2.88.3 # gobject-introspection 1.86.0_3 # gtk+3 3.24.52 GTK 3 was then verified from Python: python3 -c "import gi; gi.require_version('Gtk', '3.0'); from gi.repository import Gtk; print(Gtk.get_major_version(), Gtk.get_minor_version())" # 3 24 PART 3 — Adapting GTK 3 to GDK Quartz on macOS The first GUI launch failed because GtkShim.py required DISPLAY or WAYLAND_DISPLAY. On macOS, GTK uses the GDK Quartz backend rather than X11 or Wayland. python3 -c "import gi; gi.require_version('Gdk', '3.0'); from gi.repository import Gdk; d=Gdk.Display.get_default(); print(d)" # GdkQuartzDisplay pkg-config --variable=targets gdk-3.0 # quartz A backup of the original file was created before editing: cp bleachbit/GtkShim.py bleachbit/GtkShim.py.backup The root-window check was changed so it is not performed on Darwin: if IS_POSIX and sys.platform != 'darwin': try: if _Gdk.get_default_root_window() is None: return False, 'No default root window (display not accessible)' except Exception as e: return False, f'Display check failed: {e}' The initial display check was also changed to accept macOS/Quartz: if sys.platform == 'darwin': return True, None PART 4 — Creating the functional .app and adding the icon The functional executable was available at /Applications/BleachBit.app/Contents/MacOS/BleachBit. The official BleachBit SVG logo was used for the application icon. curl -L https://raw.githubusercontent.com/bleachbit/bleachbit-misc/master/logo-square.svg -o bleachbit-icon.svg brew install imagemagick brew install libicns magick bleachbit-icon.svg -background none -resize 512x512 PNG32:/tmp/BleachBit-512.png png2icns /tmp/BleachBit.icns /tmp/BleachBit-512.png The earlier iconutil-based ICNS generation was discarded because iconutil failed to generate the ICNS. libicns produced a valid macOS ICNS file: file /tmp/BleachBit.icns # Mac OS X icon, ... "ic09" type The icon was added to the application bundle and declared in Info.plist: mkdir -p /Applications/BleachBit.app/Contents/Resources cp /tmp/BleachBit.icns /Applications/BleachBit.app/Contents/Resources/BleachBit.icns /usr/libexec/PlistBuddy -c "Add :CFBundleIconFile string BleachBit.icns" /Applications/BleachBit.app/Contents/Info.plist PART 5 — Compiling the translations The po/ directory already contained the translation source files (.po), but no compiled .mo files were initially present. which msgfmt msgfmt --version # /opt/homebrew/bin/msgfmt # GNU gettext-tools 1.0 The existing Makefile in po/ already provided the appropriate target: make -C po local This generated the .mo files and copied them into: locale//LC_MESSAGES/bleachbit.mo A total of 61 .mo files were generated. Spanish was verified with: python3 -c "import bleachbit; print('Locale dir:', bleachbit.locale_dir)" # /Users/aba/bleachbit/locale python3 -c "import bleachbit.Language as L; print('Language:', L.get_active_language_code())" # es_ES python3 -c "from bleachbit.Language import get_text; print(get_text('Preferences'))" # Preferencias PART 6 — Integrating all 61 languages into the .app The source code in bleachbit/__init__.py was checked and confirmed to search for a local ./locale directory. The compiled translations were therefore copied into the application bundle, and the launcher was adjusted to run from Contents. cp -R ~/bleachbit/locale /Applications/BleachBit.app/Contents/ The launcher was changed to: #!/bin/zsh APP_CONTENTS="/Applications/BleachBit.app/Contents" BLEACHBIT_HOME="$HOME/bleachbit" cd "$APP_CONTENTS" || exit 1 exec "$HOME/.pyenv/versions/bleachbit-venv/bin/python3" \ "$BLEACHBIT_HOME/bleachbit.py" --gui The resulting locale path was verified: locale_dir: /Applications/BleachBit.app/Contents/locale The GUI then displayed the additional languages in Preferences, and Spanish was confirmed working. PART 7 — Ad-hoc signing and macOS extended attributes The application bundle was locally signed using an ad-hoc signature. After modifying the bundle, codesign reported Finder-related attributes that prevented signing. codesign --force --deep --sign - /Applications/BleachBit.app xattr -lr /Applications/BleachBit.app # com.apple.quarantine # com.apple.FinderInfo # com.apple.ResourceFork The extended attributes were removed and the application was signed again: xattr -cr /Applications/BleachBit.app codesign --force --deep --sign - /Applications/BleachBit.app The final verification succeeded: codesign --verify --deep --strict --verbose=2 /Applications/BleachBit.app /Applications/BleachBit.app: valid on disk /Applications/BleachBit.app: satisfies its Designated Requirement The signature inspection showed Signature=adhoc, SHA-256 and 63 sealed resources. TeamIdentifier=not set is expected for an ad-hoc signature. The resulting application is a functional BleachBit 6.0.3 build on the development Mac, with the GTK GUI running through Quartz, the application icon installed, and the translations embedded in the bundle. Final verification: codesign --verify --deep --strict --verbose=2 /Applications/BleachBit.app valid on disk satisfies its Designated Requirement PART 9 — Scope and limitations The current build is not yet a self-contained .app that can be installed on any other Mac. The launcher explicitly uses the pyenv Python environment and the source tree in the user's home directory. $HOME/.pyenv/versions/bleachbit-venv/bin/python3 $HOME/bleachbit/bleachbit.py Therefore, copying only the .app to another Mac does not guarantee that it will run. The target Mac would need the corresponding Python environment and dependencies. A portable DMG installer was deliberately not included in this procedure. Creating a genuinely standalone application would require bundling Python, PyGObject, GTK, typelibs and dynamic libraries, fixing their runtime paths, and testing the resulting bundle on a clean Mac without the development environment.

items.title: `deepscan.venv` destroys Python virtual environments used by installed applications (Anki)
items.body:
The `deepscan.venv` option recursively deletes all files inside any directory whose path matches `[/\\].?venv` — this includes `.venv` and `venv` directories found anywhere under `~`. This destroys Python virtual environments used by installed applications, not just user-created development venvs.

**Is this intended behavior?** The rule (`wholeregex="[/\\].?venv"`) has no exclusions for application directories. The scan starts from `os.path.expanduser('~')` ([`Worker.py` `clean_operation()`](https://github.com/bleachbit/bleachbit/blob/master/bleachbit/Worker.py)) and traverses into `AppData\Local` via `os.walk()` ([`DeepScan.py` `DeepScan.scan()`](https://github.com/bleachbit/bleachbit/blob/master/bleachbit/DeepScan.py)). The only directory filter is the user whitelist ([`FileUtilities.py` `whitelisted()`](https://github.com/bleachbit/bleachbit/blob/master/bleachbit/FileUtilities.py)), which is empty by default.

**Affected application: Anki (launcher versions 25.02–25.09)**

Anki 25.02–25.09 uses a launcher (`anki.exe`) that invokes `uv run anki`. The `uv` tool creates a virtual environment at `AppData\Local\AnkiProgramFiles\.venv\` containing a complete Python installation and all Anki dependencies:

- Python runtime (`python313.dll`, `python.exe`, `pythonw.exe`)
- All installed packages (PyQt6, aqt, anki, protobuf, pywin32, etc.)
- DLL dependencies (`libcrypto-3.dll`, `libssl-3.dll`, `vcruntime140.dll`)
- All `.pyd` native extensions

Total: 5,946 files, 587 MB.

The path `...\AnkiProgramFiles\.venv\...` matches the regex `[/\\].?venv` because of the `\` before `.venv`. After deletion, `uv run anki` cannot find the Python interpreter or any packages — Anki fails to launch.

**Note:** Anki 26.05+ uses embedded Python (no `.venv`) and is not affected.

**Mechanism:** `os.walk()` iterates over `filenames`, not `dirnames` ([`DeepScan.py` line ~95](https://github.com/bleachbit/bleachbit/blob/master/bleachbit/DeepScan.py)). The `wholeregex` is tested against the full path of each file ([`CompiledSearch.match()`](https://github.com/bleachbit/bleachbit/blob/master/bleachbit/DeepScan.py)). So a file at `...\AnkiProgramFiles\.venv\Lib\site-packages\anki\__init__.py` matches because the path contains `\.venv`. Each file inside a `.venv` directory is listed individually.

Additionally, the regex matches Python's own `venv` standard library module at `AppData\Roaming\uv\python\cpython-3.13.5-...\Lib\venv\` (13 files) — this is part of the Python installation itself.

**Suggestion:** Either exclude known application directories (`AppData\Local\AnkiProgramFiles`, `AppData\Roaming`), or add a warning that this option will destroy virtual environments used by installed applications — not just development venvs created by the user.

At a high level, the improvements are aimed towards....

1. Fixing the structure of the package to reduce the need to do imports inside of function calls (I assume those are currently there to fix circular import errors).
2. Adding [PEP 484-style type hints](https://peps.python.org/pep-0484/) to give editor suggestions for tab-complete and allow tools like [mypy](https://mypy.readthedocs.io/en/stable/) or [pyright](https://microsoft.github.io/pyright/#/) to catch bugs during static analysis.
3. Adding a dependency management system: even something simple like `python -m venv` in combination with a `requirements.txt` file will simplify the setup of the dev and testing environments.  A more reliable and sturdy solution would be to either implement a [PEP 517-style build system](https://peps.python.org/pep-0517/) with something like [meson](https://github.com/mesonbuild/meson) as the actual build backend or to add [conda](https://docs.conda.io/en/latest/) to the repo which can manage both python and non-python dependencies (aka gtk in this case).  This will eventually remove the need for the fragile build scripts made specifically for this project and just allow bleachbit to use well-specced standards.
4. Removing deprecated code, fixing excessively nested/awkward conditionals, using comprehension over for-loops where possible, switching to use of generators (functions with `yield`) over for loops where possible, and other optimizations.
5. IF all of the above 4 are done, I speculate that a reliable and most importantly maintainable **MacOS build with GUI** is possible.  I know that it has been a requested feature for a long time, judging by the website and some of the other issues.

To clarify, I am **ready** and **able** to start submitting pull requests to gradually merge the proposed changes (gotta implement them first).  I understand how important maintaining high coverage % and minimizing regressions is to a project like this, so I indend to make my PRs small and do this in small segments over time.  I have also already read the docs and contribution guide.  However, I have a couple clarifying questions to the current maintainers: 

1. What is the targeted minimum version for python support?  Currently, the earliest version that is not officially end-of-life is 3.8.  However, in this repo I see some code suitable for versions which are much older.  The features I suggested above would work for 3.6 and up.
2. What are the near term milestones and existing plans (if any) for development and new features?  I want to work with you around your existing goals as much as possible and not cause confusion.  

Thank you for taking the time to read through this!  And again thank you for your work in maintaining this project.

items.title: Missing icons with 2265 Python 3.10 build with natively installed vcruntime140.dll
items.body:
I found two consecutive and related bugs with the latest 2265 build using an already installed Visual C++ 2015-2022 Redistributable package in a Windows 11 VM. With regards to #1407, the 2015 Redistributable is what specifically provides the necessary vcruntime140.dll to run the build. This report will cover the first bug.

**Steps to reproduce the behavior**
1. Make sure to have (at least) the Visual C++ 2015 Redistributable installed.
2. Download [BleachBit-4.4.2.2265-setup-English.exe](https://ci.bleachbit.org/dl/4.4.2.2265-mkhon-python310/BleachBit-4.4.2.2265-setup-English.exe).
3. Run installer, keep clicking next to install.
4. Open the application the first time. Accept the Windows UAC (User Account Control) if prompted.
5. See the applicable screenshot for the result.

**Expected behavior**
Should look as if running it in Linux with the icons provided by the Adwaita theme.

**Screenshot**
![bug](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/101818165/196367970-5d83f445-e1bd-4f7b-aecd-5efa12f49967.png)

**Desktop Specs**
 - OS: Windows 11 (via qemu-kvm using virt-manager to manage passthrough configurations)
 - BleachBit 4.4.2.2265
